[page[title]]

Represent, schedule and execute long-running or composed business processes with visible state.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Flow definitions, instances, events and progress APIs.
  • Reusable activities for APIs, documents, templates, transformations and flow control.
  • Queued execution, scheduled tasks, maintenance and repair through hosted services and an execution engine.

Why the boundary matters

Multi-step work becomes inspectable business state instead of a chain of hidden background calls.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.Workflow on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Workflow" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddWorkflowWeb(/* platform configuration */);
app.StartWorkflowWeb();

// Execution workers additionally register:
builder.Services.AddWorkflowEngine();

Configure and run it

Configure persistence, Eventing, the workflow API route and the activity set required by the host. HostedServices and Workflow execution hosts should use the corresponding registration/startup path so queues, schedules and repair work have clear ownership.

Consume the capability

Define flows and activities, create FlowInstanceData, and observe progress through WorkflowEvent records. Prefer the engine and activity abstractions over directly chaining background calls so long-running state remains inspectable.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.Workflow.git
cd cCoder.Workflow
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
